en: The Eight Verses of Homage to Mahābodhi.
He who possesses a golden complexion, a voice like the kalaviṅka bird, and the voice of Brahmā; who is compassionate and most worthy of service.
I pay homage to the Supreme among Men, whose body is purified by ethical discipline, the glorious Mahābodhi. || 1 ||

I bow to the glorious Mahābodhi—the Lord of Victors who arose from the lineage of the Śākya King, whose divine body severs craving and pierces Māra, who is the locus of primordial wisdom, who destroys the afflictions, and who is like the sun. (2)

I pay homage to the glorious Mahābodhi—Samantabhadra, whose limbs possess the excellent marks, who accomplishes the welfare of beings through his virtuous deeds, who is worthy of salutation, and whose mind is solely intent on the benefit of sentient beings as the source of all prosperity. (3)

I pay homage to that glorious Mahābodhi, the cloud of perfect enlightenment who, out of compassion, released the water of the Dharma for the sake of the happiness of those individuals inflamed by the fire of passion. (4)

I bow to the glorious Mahābodhi, the Tathāgata who is the bridge for crossing the ocean of existence, the knower of reality, the lion among men, the lord of the three worlds, and the jewel of supreme enlightenment. (5)

I bow to the glorious Mahābodhi—the Teacher, the foremost among excellent bodhisattvas, the son of Māyā who stands firm in his vows to accomplish the welfare of all beings, the conqueror of Māra, and the vanquisher of enemies. 6.
I bow to the glorious Mahābodhi, the Lord of Lokeśa, the Lord of Harinātha, the Lord of Bhūteśa, the Lord of Suranātha, the Lord of Kṛtānta, and the Lord of Naranātha. (7)
He is the form of the Buddha, he is indeed the form of the Dharma, and he alone is the Saṅgha for those to be trained;
he was the refuge for those who had come for refuge—I bow to the glorious Great Enlightenment. 8.
